transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Um… I guess I’m here because my sleep has gotten pretty bad lately. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but it’s kind of fallen apart. I’ll be in bed at my apartment for hours, laptop already closed, and I’m still mentally going back over work deadlines, tuition payments, class assignments… like I can’t shut it off. And even when I do sleep, I wake up feeling like I never really rested. Does that make sense?
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or worried even when you're not trying to fall asleep?

Yeah… I mean, I try not to let it take over, but yes. It’s not only at bedtime. During the day my mind just kind of jumps around—like, am I falling behind at work, am I wasting money on school, is my family going to think I can’t handle things. And then even a small issue starts to feel like it could mess up everything long-term. I know that probably sounds a little excessive, but that’s kind of how it feels.
Have you noticed yourself feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, even when there’s no specific reason for it?

Um… I don’t think so, not really. I mean, I have days where I feel kind of worn out or not very upbeat, but I wouldn’t say I’m just sad for no reason or that I’ve stopped caring about things I usually like. At least, I haven’t noticed that in a major way. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you noticed any physical symptoms, like restlessness, feeling on edge, fatigue, or muscle tension, especially when you're worrying about these things?

Yeah… I guess fatigue is probably the main thing I’ve noticed. I don’t want to overstate it, but by midafternoon at the office I feel completely drained—like even answering emails feels harder than it should, or walking to the subway takes real effort. And then I’ll think, okay, I’ll rest on the weekend and catch up, but it doesn’t really feel like I get my energy back. Is that what you mean?
Have you found it harder to focus or concentrate on tasks lately, like reading through an email or following a conversation?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I can still get things done, but it takes me way longer than it should. I’ll be staring at the same financial model at work or a reading for class, and then realize I’ve read the same paragraph like five times and none of it actually stuck. My mind is already off going through everything that could go wrong. I don’t know if that counts as trouble concentrating, but that’s been happening.
Have you noticed yourself getting more irritable or easily annoyed lately, even over small things?

Um… I don’t think so? Not in a way that feels really obvious to me. I mean, I probably get a little short when I’m already stressed, but I try not to take it out on people. I wouldn’t say I’m snapping at everyone or anything like that. Is that something I should be paying closer attention to?
Do you find that your worrying feels excessive or hard to control, even when you know it might not be necessary?

Yeah… I think that’s probably fair to say. I try to tell myself, like, “Okay, stop, just focus on this one thing,” but then it kind of jumps to the next thing and the next. I’ll end up checking my calendar again, then my budget, then my assignments, over and over… and I know at a certain point it’s not really helping, but it’s hard to stop. And then I’m not actually getting the thing done, which makes me feel worse. Does that make sense?
